originalGoal.statement: Owner can leave the computer for long periods while TSF continues useful, bounded engineering work without drifting from the original goal, across seven upgrades that turn TSF into a real daily-driver planner/autonomy layer over Orca.
sevenUpgrades: M1: Project Onboarding V1 -- Add Project -> Analyze -> Health -> Direction -> Upgrade Backlog -> Known/Active/Work Set
M2: Keep Going / Overnight V1 -- real project-level long-run controller over Orca (highest priority)
M3: Chat -> Dispatch + Live Work Feed -- Planner Chat becomes operational, not just conversational
M4: Run Journal + Recovery -- durable run timeline, restart recovery, no repeated settled work
M5: Capacity-Aware Routing -- route around provider capacity without manual meter-watching
M6: Desktop TSF -- double-click launch, no manual localhost/terminal management
M7: Project Memory V2 -- durable selective memory (facts/decisions/preferences/lessons) across planner sessions

waves.summary: First application of the new EXPIRING_CAPACITY policy (capacityPolicy.expiringCapacityRule) and this program's first real live Orca dispatch. Codex was ~5.75h from its weekly reset with ~9% capacity remaining -- treated as expiring inventory per the new rule and assigned exactly the bounded task already queued as nextSafeAction: extend tsf/adapters/orca-runtime.mjs with mapOrchestrationFacts(facts), a pure projection of real worker-list/task-list/gate-list output into workerHeartbeats/resultCapsules/openGates. Dispatched via `orca terminal create --worktree active --command codex` in the current worktree (no new worktree/heavy install, to avoid stranding risk within the capacity window) with a hard-scoped prompt (two files only, no CLI mutation, no commit). Worker ran real read-only orca CLI inspection (worker-list/task-list/gate-list/run-list --json against pre-existing run run_79578caf1acb) to ground field names in the actual output shape rather than guessing, implemented the projection, added tsf/test/orca-runtime.test.mjs (3 tests), and self-reported 118/118 GREEN + clean oxlint/oxfmt in 14m31s. Independently re-verified by the planner session (VERIFIER_INDEPENDENT, separate identity from the Codex worker): git diff reviewed line by line (workerHeartbeats correctly returns lastHeartbeatAt: null rather than fabricating a timestamp the real worker-list output doesn't have; resultCapsules correctly uses validateResultCapsule to filter out non-TSF-shaped raw worker reports rather than upgrading them; openGates field names cross-checked against a real live `task-list --json` sample confirming the CLI's snake_case convention, not guessed), full suite re-run independently (118/118 GREEN), oxlint/oxfmt re-run independently (both clean). Scope held exactly to the two authorized files -- no commit/staging performed by the worker, matching instructions. After completion, Codex's own in-session UI showed an 'approaching rate limits' model-downgrade prompt; per the policy's shrink-and-stop rule, no second task was queued this wave even though several hours remained before reset -- checkpointing here instead.

directives: Continue autonomously without routine check-ins for the remainder of this window.
Prioritize completing M2 Keep Going / Overnight V1 to a genuinely GREEN, verified, locally-adopted state if safely possible.
If M2 finishes with substantial time remaining, proceed into M3 per the existing program charter.
Aggressively use otherwise-expiring Claude/Codex capacity on useful bounded work that can safely finish before the cutoff (extends capacityPolicy.expiringCapacityRule for this window specifically).
Do not manufacture work merely to consume tokens.
Preserve only a small reserve sufficient to finish, verify, fence, and checkpoint active work.
Shrink task size as 11:20 PM approaches.
Do not begin a major new architecture wave close to the cutoff if it cannot reasonably settle before Tim returns.
Do not pause early merely to conserve capacity -- maximum useful safe progress before 11:20 PM, then a clean handoff.
returnHandoffModeRequirements: Allow safely finishable active bounded work to settle.
Run the appropriate tests/checks for completed work.
Record current provider capacity/reset state if trustworthy.
Leave no unnecessary dev servers/heavy workers running.
Preserve any candidate awaiting adoption exactly.
operatorReturnBriefMustCover: provider state after reset if observable
the single best next action for Tim
exact prompt/instruction to resume autonomous mode later if desired
executionWindow.preservedConstraints: All existing architecture, authority, Windows-safety, real-project, and local-adoption rules (Sections B/F/G/H/I) remain in force unchanged -- this window sets pacing and priority only, not new authority.

expiringCapacityRule.statement: Owner preference: use available provider capacity rather than leaving substantial capacity unused before a known reset, without straying from bounded/safe/independently-verified execution discipline.
expiringCapacityRule.trigger: A provider reports a known reset window (resetsAt/reset description) via a live capacity check, with meaningful capacity remaining before that reset.
rules: Treat remaining capacity as expiring inventory, not something to conserve past the reset.

Preferentially assign small, bounded, independently useful tasks to that provider: focused implementation, tests, verifier passes, documentation reconciliation, bounded research, fixture work, or isolated repairs.
Choose only tasks that can reasonably finish and checkpoint before exhaustion or reset, whichever comes first.
Do not start a large critical-path task likely to be stranded mid-flight merely to consume capacity.
Never manufacture useless work just to consume tokens -- if no useful bounded work exists, leave the capacity unused.
Keep a small safety reserve sufficient to finish/fence/checkpoint whatever is currently in flight.
As reset approaches, progressively shrink the size of newly assigned tasks.
Once usable capacity is effectively exhausted, checkpoint and wait/switch providers normally -- do not force further dispatch.
Immediately after reset, reassess live capacity and restore the normal worker budget/concurrency for that provider.
appliesToProviders: any future provider with a known reset window
expiringCapacityRule.supersedesForNearResetWindowOnly: The general 'hold off on new WORKER_* dispatch near a limit' base policy above -- this amendment only relaxes that base policy inside a known-reset window with a genuine bounded task available; it does not authorize dispatch when no such task exists or when the task risks stranding.
mustStillHonor: Section F execution discipline (conflict-aware waves, independent verification, no worker self-report treated as done)
Section H adoption checklist for anything reaching adoption
